notes: This card documents allomorphs with missing or insufficient evidence; it is never presented as source-backed support.

The single evidence gate (_extension_is_evidence_gated) is applied to generation and to inferred analyzer derivations alike, so a reviewed base lemma cannot authorize a restricted derivation on either side.

The supported path for an attested derived form is to publish it as its own reviewed verb-stem lemma; exact lexical analysis and search then serve it without asserting an unverified derivational relationship.

Causative -idz-/-edz- shape and vowel conditioning are attested (Fortune (d); Hannan pp. 158, 240), but which lemma takes -idz- versus -is- is a per-lemma semantic choice; Fortune defers that distribution to section 4.2.6.3.2 (not available).
Hannan derives -ts- surfaces only via radical mutation (e.g. -muk- + -y- -> -muts-); no -its-/-ets- extension allomorph is attested.
Hannan printed p. xii lists -ura among single verb suffixes, but no entry with conditioning or base pairs was located; Fortune attests no short reversive.
Promote entries out of this card only with a verified locator backing the per-lemma distribution; until then the allomorphs stay excluded from generation and from inferred analyses.

qa.reviewer_notes: 2026-09-09 correction pass: reciprocal moved out to its own evidence-backed card (fortune.verbal.reciprocal.001); dz/ts and short reversive generation switched from warning to structured refusal, with Hannan locators added for the -idz-/-edz- shape. 2026-09-09 supervisor-blocker follow-up: the same gate now excludes these derivations from analyzer candidates, so the card is no longer consumed by the analyzer as a derivation rule. Not an independent human linguistic review.

rule_summary: Evidence-gated extension allomorphs: causative -idz-/-edz- (style dz), causative -its-/-ets- (style ts), and short reversive -ur-/-or- (style short). Neither the generator nor the analyzer presents an inferred derivation through these allomorphs: a reviewed base lemma is not evidence for a restricted derivation. Attested surfaces resolve only when the full form is published as its own reviewed verb-stem lemma.
source_locator: Fortune, Shona Grammatical Constructions Vol. 1 (1985), section 2.10.2.3.3 (d), PDF p. 33 (printed p. 21): -idz- ~ -edz- shape attested with radical mutations (e.g. -muk- + -y- -> -muts-); distribution deferred to section 4.2.6.3.2 (not in the available volume). Hannan dictionary: printed p. 158, '-edza KKoMZ v sfx > causative ext of R containing e or o; kuenda > kuendedza'; printed p. 240, '-idza KKoMZ v sfx > a causative ext of R; kubvuma > kubvumidza'. Short reversive: Hannan printed p. xii lists -ura among single verb suffixes, but no dictionary entry with its conditioning or base pairs was located; Fortune attests no short reversive. -its-/-ets-: no locator in any available source.
